To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aging is a factor that influences oral tolerance and that it is possible to induce oral tolerance in old rats by using a high frequency feeding protocol.
aging affects the establishment of oral antigen-specific tolerance in mice and the immunoglobulin isotypic pattern of specific antibodies produced by tolerant and immunocompetent mice.

aging affects the establishment of oral immunologic tolerance and that the immunoglobulin isotypic pattern of specific antibodies formed in the course of oral tolerance is dependent upon the animal's age, the antigen's molecular size, and the frequency of oral antigen administration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms involved in the establishment of oral immune responses and tolerance.
the study of the immunological phenomena associated with the establishment of oral immunologic tolerance and the influence of aging on these events.
the study of oral tolerance and the immunoglobulin isotypic patterns of the antibodies produced in the course of oral tolerance and immunization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
oral tolerance is not a single phenomenon, but a set of different phenomena that are affected differently by age.
aging affects oral tolerance and that oral administration of antigens may induce different immunoglobulin isotypic patterns in tolerant and immunized individuals.
aging is not an important factor for the establishment and maintenance of oral tolerance, but it does affect the isotypic patterns of specific antibodies formed in tolerant and immunized mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immunoglobulin isotypic patterns are not a good indicator for oral tolerance, but they can help to identify the pathways of B cell interactions leading to oral tolerance and immunization.
aging is associated with a decreased ability to induce oral tolerance and with a shift in isotypic patterns of specific antibodies.

oral tolerance is a complex phenomenon which depends on many factors, and that the isotypic profile of the antibody response to an orally administered antigen may be a valuable parameter for assessing the establishment of oral immunologic unresponsiveness.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the immunoglobulin isotypic profile of the antibodies formed in response to oral administration of antigen is not a simple reflection of the immunoglobulin class switch mechanism, as it is the case for antibodies formed in the course of a systemic immunization.
oral tolerance is an age-related process that is influenced by other factors such as the frequency of feeding.
aging is associated with changes in the immune system, which in turn affect the development of oral tolerance.
